americancurl: An American curl cat sitting, a medium silky-coated cat whose one distinguishing feature is its EARS: they are set wide on the head and CURVE SMOOTHLY BACKWARD AND OUTWARD IN A FIRM ARC, the tips sweeping back toward the centre of the skull instead of standing up, each ear opening turned forward and lined with long tufts of pale fur. Walnut-shaped eyes, a plumed tail.
anatolianshepherd: An Anatolian shepherd dog standing, a very large heavy-boned livestock guardian dog with a broad deep chest, long straight legs and a thick neck. Its short dense coat is plain pale SANDY FAWN, and its face carries a SOOTY BLACK MASK across the muzzle and around the eyes with small drop ears of the same black. Its tail is long and carried in a loose curve.
angorarabbit: An Angora rabbit, a rabbit almost entirely BURIED IN AN ENORMOUS MASS OF LONG SILKY WHITE WOOL that hangs well past its feet and swallows the outline of its body into a single round cloud, so that only a small flat FACE, a black nose and two dark eyes show through the fringe. Its ears are short and tipped with long trailing tufts.
cornishrex: A Cornish rex cat standing, a very slender fine-boned cat with a deeply ARCHED BACK, a tucked waist and long thin legs, so its silhouette curves like a bow. Its coat is EXTREMELY SHORT AND LIES IN CLOSE REGULAR WASHBOARD WAVES all over the body, with no long guard hairs. Very large upright ears set high, a narrow egg-shaped head, and prominent cheekbones.
egyptianmau: An Egyptian mau cat standing, a lithe medium cat with a SILVER-GREY COAT MARKED ALL OVER WITH SMALL DISTINCT RANDOM BLACK SPOTS on the flanks and belly, banded rings on the legs and tail, and a DARK M-SHAPED MARK ON ITS FOREHEAD with two lines curving back across the cheek. Its eyes are LARGE, SLIGHTLY WORRIED-LOOKING AND GOOSEBERRY GREEN.
burmese: A Burmese cat sitting, a compact surprisingly heavy medium cat with a rounded skull, full cheeks, and a short straight muzzle with a firm chin. Its coat is VERY SHORT, CLOSE-LYING AND SATIN-GLOSSY in a warm even SABLE BROWN, darkening slightly on the face and ears, and its EYES ARE LARGE, ROUND AND DEEP GOLDEN-YELLOW.
manx: A Manx cat standing in side view, a round compact cat with a distinctly ROUNDED RUMP AND NO TAIL AT ALL, the back ending in a smooth curve. Its HIND LEGS ARE NOTICEABLY LONGER THAN ITS FRONT LEGS so the rump stands higher than the shoulders and the back slopes upward toward the rear. Round head, round eyes, a dense double coat in tabby brown.
munchkin: A Munchkin cat standing in side view, a cat of ordinary head and body size carried on LEGS ONLY ABOUT HALF THE NORMAL LENGTH, so its chest sits very close to the ground and its body looks long and low. The shortening is in the upper limb bones, so the legs are short but straight and evenly proportioned. Medium coat, upright ears, a long tail held up.
frenchbulldog: A French bulldog standing facing forward, a small heavy compact dog with a broad square chest and a short thick body. Its head is LARGE AND SQUARE WITH A VERY FLAT SHORT MUZZLE, a deeply folded wrinkle across the nose, and prominent round dark eyes set wide and low. Its ears are the marking that names it: LARGE, UPRIGHT, BROAD AT THE BASE AND ROUNDED AT THE TOP like a bat's.
bullterrier: A bull terrier standing in side view, a muscular medium dog with a deep barrel chest and short strong legs. Its head is the point: seen from the side the top of the skull and the muzzle form ONE CONTINUOUS UNBROKEN DOWNWARD CURVE FROM EAR TO NOSE WITH NO DIP AT ALL BETWEEN THE EYES, an even egg shape. Small dark TRIANGULAR SLANTED EYES set close, small erect ears, short white coat.
domesticfox: A domesticated silver fox sitting, a fox with the marks of tameness rather than a wild fox: its coat is dark silver-grey BROKEN BY IRREGULAR WHITE PIEBALD PATCHES across the face, chest and paws, one EAR IS SOFT AND FLOPPY while the other stands up, its muzzle is shorter and rounder than a wild fox's, and its bushy tail CURLS UP AND OVER ITS BACK.
englishbudgie: An English show budgerigar, a budgie noticeably LARGER AND HEAVIER THAN A WILD ONE, with a big rounded head and a DENSE PUFFED MASS OF FEATHERS OVER THE FOREHEAD AND CROWN that swells out above and partly hoods the eyes, so the skull looks broad and domed. Its body is deep and wide through the chest, plumage sky-blue and white with fine black barring on the wings.
fancypigeon: A fancy fantail pigeon standing, a small white pigeon with an ERECT ROUNDED CHEST THRUST HIGH AND FORWARD and its head tipped back to almost touch its tail. Its tail is the point: A LARGE FLAT FAN OF THIRTY OR MORE STIFF FEATHERS HELD FULLY SPREAD AND UPRIGHT like an open peacock's fan, far broader than its body. Short legs, feathered feet.
ballpythonmorph: A piebald ball python, a stout heavy-bodied python of moderate length in a loose relaxed S. Its pattern is the point: LARGE IRREGULAR AREAS OF PURE UNMARKED WHITE alternate with patches of normal python markings in gold, chocolate-brown and black, the boundaries sharp and ragged like torn paper, so the animal reads as two snakes joined. Small head, heat pits along the lip.
bredaxolotl: A leucistic axolotl, a pale aquatic salamander with a smooth PINKISH-WHITE translucent body, a broad flat head, a WIDE PERMANENTLY SMILING MOUTH and small dark eyes. From behind its head spread THREE PAIRS OF FEATHERY EXTERNAL GILL STALKS OF BRIGHT BLOOD-RED FILAMENTS, held out like fans. Four small delicate legs with fine fingers, and a long finned tail.
silkworm: A silkworm, the plump soft CATERPILLAR of the silk moth: a smooth segmented grub about the length of a finger, CREAMY IVORY-WHITE all over, its body divided into a dozen deep fleshy folds, with a small brown head capsule, several pairs of short stubby fleshy prolegs beneath, and a SMALL BLUNT CURVED HORN ON THE TAIL SEGMENT.
